neighbours.label: a word inside a set phrase whose next word is all but fixed ('a whole new [light]', 'the most famous [of all]'); the same words outside the set phrase stay low
fire: After the trip she saw her hometown in a whole new light.
Moving abroad opened up a whole new world for the children.
Of all the lighthouses on the coast, this is the oldest of all.
He is perhaps the greatest climber of all time.
The remodel gave the old barn a whole new look.
That winter was the coldest of all the winters she remembered.
The new coach brought a whole new attitude to the team.
Many call it the strangest mystery of all.
quiet: After the trip she painted her hometown in soft evening light.
Moving abroad was hard at first for the children.
This lighthouse on the coast was built in the last century.
He is a strong climber who trains every weekend.
The remodel gave the old barn a new roof and doors.
That winter was cold, and the river froze in January.
The new coach brought fresh players to the team.
Many call it a strange case that nobody solved.
